summary.oneLiner: Strong Q4 FY26 performance driven by pellet and rolled product ramp-up, with EBITDA margin holding at 23% despite softer realizations; key catalysts are the 20GW BESS, 1Mn ton integrated steel plant, and 540MW solar expansion, positioning GPIL as a vertically integrated low-carbon steel and energy transition player.

one-line thesis: Strong Q4 FY26 performance driven by pellet and rolled product ramp-up, with EBITDA margin holding at 23% despite softer realizations; key catalysts are the 20GW BESS, 1Mn ton integrated steel plant, and 540MW solar expansion, positioning GPIL as a vertically integrated low-carbon steel and energy transition player.
financial scorecard: revenue: INR 5,200cr (FY26), +41% QoQ in Q4; EBITDA/margin: INR 1,253cr (FY26), 23% margin; PAT (rptd): INR 802cr (FY26), impacted by de-recognition of Ardent stake; PAT (normalized): ~INR 900cr (excl. one-off gains/losses); order book: 6 months for structural rolled products; net debt: net cash position of INR 837cr
guidance: revenue growth: >INR 6,000cr in FY27; margin: 24-25% EBITDA margin; order inflow: 20GW BESS (commissioning Mar’27), 1Mn ton steel plant (construction Oct’26); capex/commissioning: 540MW solar (55MW commissioned, 100MW by Jul’26), 2Mn ton pellet plant (Dec’25), CRM (Mar’27), BESS (Mar’27), Ari Dongri mine expansion (FY28)
order book & pipeline: 6 months for structural rolled products; long-term BESS supply agreements signed with EVE and Roche; no explicit order book for steel plant yet
segment / subsidiary detail: Pellets: 4.7Mn ton capacity (2Mn ton new plant commissioned Dec’25); Sponge iron: 0.65Mn ton capacity (up from 0.59Mn ton); Structural rolled: 3.75L tons FY27 target; BESS: 20GW project (Phase 1: 5-6GW FY28); Solar: 540MW total (165MW existing + 125MW by Jul’26); Mining: 4Mn ton ore mined FY26 (3.4Mn ton usable post-beneficiation)
growth verticals / optionality: 20GW BESS (INR 15,000cr revenue potential); 1Mn ton integrated steel plant (INR 6,000cr revenue potential); CRM (INR 3,000-4,000cr revenue); Boria Tibu mine expansion to 4Mn ton (FY30); potential new mine auctions
margins & cost dynamics: Pellet margin: INR 2,000/ton conversion cost; DRI: 40% iron ore, 35% coal, 25% opex; BESS margin: 12-13% currently (conservative 7-8% assumed); mining cost: INR 3,000-3,200/ton; freight saving: INR 150/ton post-beneficiation at mine
capex / expansion: Total capex: ~INR 7,000cr for integrated steel plant; INR 1,500cr for BESS; INR 800cr for solar expansion; INR 500cr for CRM; INR 300cr for mine beneficiation plant; total FY26-28 capex >INR 10,000cr
capital allocation: Net cash position INR 837cr; capex prioritized for BESS, steel plant, solar; no dividend policy mentioned; focus on debt-free growth and vertical integration
risks & watch-items: Iron ore price volatility; BESS component cost inflation (lithium); delays in steel plant commissioning; export market access; regulatory delays in environmental clearances; global steel demand slowdown
management quality / tone: Confident, forward-looking, and execution-focused; transparent on CAPEX revisions; emphasizes decarbonization, export readiness, and vertical integration; acknowledges Q1 price softening but remains bullish on long-term demand
non-obvious takeaways: BESS margins are higher than initially modeled (12-13% vs 7-8%) due to Indian grid instability demand; EV fleet adoption cut diesel costs by 75% and emissions by 88%; pellet premium pricing will emerge post-monsoon (Q3) as high-grade output rises; INR 100cr CAPEX saved by switching from coal gasification to natural gas for pellets

themes.title: Metals & mining cycle - steel, aluminium, critical minerals
themes.need: Domestic demand growth, safeguard duties and an India capacity-expansion wave lift integrated metals while critical-mineral security gains policy support. TATASTEEL targets 45-50 MT India (FY26 India EBITDA INR34,272cr at 24% margin) with a +INR6,000/t 1QFY27 realisation uplift; JINDALSTEL/SAIL/JSWSTEEL-tier on steel; HINDALCO/NALCO on aluminium; HINDZINC on zinc (Q1FY27 all-time-record EBITDA INR8,074cr +109% YoY on a record-low zinc cost-of-production USD851/t, though CEO Arun Misra hands over to ex-SAIL chief Amarendu Prakash 1-Aug-2026 and a new Gundlupet REE/Yttrium critical-minerals block won this quarter is a 2031-32-dated option, not near-term); NMDC/COALINDIA/LLOYDSME/SARDAEN on iron-ore/coal/integrated mining. Q1FY27 also quantified the export-side shock and the downstream escape from it: JINDALSAW's consolidated PAT fell 78% YoY to INR 91cr on +9% revenue because the Strait-of-Hormuz blockade suspended ALL India-origin MENA export shipments from March 2026, holding utilisation at ~60-65%; SHYAMMETL took the other route, posting INR 5,455cr revenue (+23.3%) at a multi-quarter-high 14.9% EBITDA margin with aluminium EBITDA/t +52% YoY and specialty alloys near 20.5% margin, self-funding ~INR 9,580cr of balance capex with no debt.
themes.driver: Steel price/realisation uplift into Q1; safeguard-duty support; Hormuz reopening for line-pipe exports; value-added/downstream mix; iron-ore + critical-mineral volume ramp.
